column2: Retain Moab's breaking faith with Israel after Ahab's death. The political breach expressed by atheteo is not made into a general moral judgment on individual Moabites, and the selected sequence remains.

Retain the lattice, upper room, Samaria, illness and inquiry about recovery. Baal Fly follows the selected name-plus-fly wording without substituting another conventional name; the final going to inquire through him remains, with the pronoun's mediation referent unresolved.
column3: How should the construction en te Baal myian and the final through him be explained without treating Baal Fly as a fully settled name analysis?

column2: Retain the Lord's angel, Elijah the Tishbite, Ahaziah king of Samaria and the negative rhetorical question about God in Israel. You in the question is plural, addressed to the messengers; no divine-address forms apply to either human recipient.

Propose Not so! for It shall not be so! because ouch houtos is an elliptical denial without an expressed future verb. The following For, the bed, denial of coming down, there and emphatic death remain, as does Elijah's actual going and speaking.
column3: The precise referent of Not so remains open; this proposal removes an unsupported future formulation without supplying an explanation of the denial.

column2: Retain the messengers' return and the king's question why they returned. The pronouns are clear from the sending sequence; no statement that they reached Ekron is added.

Propose Not so! consistently with verse 4 for the repeated elliptical denial. Retain the man's meeting, return command, full reported oracle and emphatic death. The question here uses singular you for the king, unlike the messengers' plural question in verse 3.
column3: The report compresses several speech levels without modern nested quotation marks; its exact punctuation remains editorial, and Not so has an unresolved antecedent.

column2: Retain the king's question about the man's character provisionally for krisis, followed by the meeting and spoken words. The answer gives physical characteristics, so character must not be treated as a settled moral evaluation.
column3: Would appearance or distinguishing description better express krisis in light of the physical answer, and what lexical evidence supports that choice?

column2: Retain a hairy man and a leather belt around the waist, followed by the identification of Elijah. The selected adjective describes the man; a garment of hair is not inserted as its exclusive explanation.

Propose and behold, Elijah was for and there Elijah was to preserve the explicit presentative at the mountain-top discovery. The commander/captain of fifty, fifty men, royal summons and descent command remain; the king has summoned is not changed into a simple says. Remove the inherited comma between was and sitting in the revised clause.

Retain the conditional identification as a man of God and future fire will come down and consume, followed by the fulfillment. The futures are not converted into imperative wishes; both the captain and his fifty are named in the prediction and event.

Retain the king's repeated sending, another captain with fifty, the ascent and the intensified command to descend quickly. Again is supported by the added sending construction; ordinary human address remains.

Retain the repeated conditional and future fire statement in full, followed by fire from heaven consuming the captain and his fifty. No of God is inserted after fire in this selected wording, and the repetition is not abbreviated.

Retain the third captain and fifty, kneeling and pleading, and the request that his life and the fifty slaves' lives be honored in Elijah's eyes. Plural English lives naturally expresses the collective singular soul of the fifty; the addressee is a human man of God.

Retain Behold, the first two captains and their fifty men, and the renewed plea for the slaves' lives. The selected final plea concerns your slaves, not only my life; But now gives a natural contrast with the preceding destruction without claiming a separate adversative particle.

Retain the angel's instruction to descend with him and not fear them, preserving singular escort and plural feared group. Elijah's rising and going down to the king fulfill the instruction; no claim of fear actually experienced is added.

Propose Not so! for the third elliptical denial, consistent with verses 4 and 6. Retain the direct why-send question, Baal Fly inquiry, bed warning and emphatic death. This version does not repeat the no God in Israel clause, so it is not supplied.

Retain the short death fulfillment according to the Lord's word spoken by Elijah. No accession date, brother relationship or lack-of-son explanation is imported into this shorter selected verse; the following lettered notice carries its own accession information.

Retain Ahaziah's remaining acts, all he did, the presentative and rhetorical annals question. The book of daily records for the kings is a source title description, not a claim that an extant modern book has been identified.

Retain the historical present reigns, Ahab as Jehoram's father, twelve years in Samaria and Jehoshaphat's eighteenth year. Beginning supplies the natural relation of accession year to reign length; the lettered unit is not merged into verse 17.

Retain the evil evaluation with the qualifications not as his brothers and not as his mother. Brothers is plural in the selected text; it is not replaced with father or brother to harmonize the notice.

Retain removal and shattering of plural Baal pillars made by his father, alongside clinging to Jeroboam's house's sins. Both the positive cultic action and the negative failure to turn away remain, without smoothing the mixed assessment.
Retain the Lord's anger directed against Ahab's house. Was stirred to anger idiomatically represents the anger construction without inventing an external agent who provoked Him in this clause.

Retain the Lord's taking up, tumult and as into heaven, with Elijah and Elisha leaving Gilgal. About to interprets the narrative introduction's timing; tumult does not identify a whirlwind, and as is not deleted to make a more familiar unqualified ascent statement.
column3: What physical force does sysseismos denote here, and how should hos eis ton ouranon be understood without imposing a later cosmological explanation?

column2: Retain the polite request to stay, sending as far as Bethel and the oath by the Lord's and Elijah's lives. I will not leave expresses the negative force of the elliptical oath introduced by if; human as you live does not take divine Thou.

Retain the Bethel prophetic sons, today's taking of your master from above your head, Elisha's knowledge and silence command. Lord and master distinguish the two referents; the head image is not replaced with a general departure.

Retain the repeated stay request, Jericho destination, two-part life oath and refusal to abandon. The variation in Greek leave/abandon verbs is expressed with the same natural will not leave formula without changing its emphatic promise.

Retain the Jericho group approaching and repeating the taking-from-above-head question. Indeed, I too preserves the strengthened acknowledgment before the same command for silence; the repetition is not removed as redundant.

Retain the third stay request, the Jordan destination, life oath and refusal, followed by both men going on. Both is explicit and prevents confusion with the watching prophetic group in the next unit.

Retain fifty prophetic sons standing opposite at a distance and both Elijah and Elisha beside the Jordan. The observers remain distinct from the pair at the river; the selected clause does not require adding that the fifty crossed with them.

Retain the sheepskin, rolling, striking and two-sided division, followed by both men crossing on barren ground. Barren is provisional for en eremo and is not silently replaced with a Greek adjective meaning dry, though dryness is naturally inferred from the crossing.
column3: Would on dry ground be a warranted contextual rendering of en eremo here, or would it erase the selected desolate/barren lexical image?

column2: Retain the request before Elijah is taken up and Elisha's double portion of your spirit upon me. Portion supplies English support for dipla; the expression is not expanded into twice the power or a detailed firstborn-inheritance explanation.
column3: Does double portion adequately preserve the unusual dipla en pneumati sou construction without deciding its social or charismatic interpretation?

column2: Retain the difficulty of the request, the condition of seeing Elijah taken up and the strongly negative alternative. It will be so and certainly will not happen preserve both outcomes rather than turning the answer into an unconditional promise.

Retain their walking and speaking, the presentative, chariot and horses of fire, separation of the two, and ascent in tumult as into heaven. The text does not explicitly put Elijah in the chariot; that familiar scene detail is not supplied.

Retain Elisha's seeing and repeated Father, singular Israel's chariot and its horseman, the loss of sight and tearing clothes into two pieces. Horseman is singular in the selected text, and Father is human address rather than divine prayer.

Retain lifting the sheepskin that fell upon Elisha, the repeated Elisha name and return to the Jordan's edge. The selected upon wording is not replaced with a simple fall from Elijah, although that is naturally inferred from the narrative.

Retain the first strike with no separation, the God-of-Elijah question with Appho, and the second strike followed by division and crossing. Appho is an unresolved transliterated element, not an approved divine name or a confident equivalent of now/where.
column3: What is the function of affo/Appho and its relation to the question; should its capitalization or punctuation change after specialist review?

column2: Retain the Jericho prophets' observation, their declaration that Elijah's spirit rests on Elisha, meeting and bowing to the ground. The human recipient of prostration is not converted into an act directed to God, and no independent narrator explanation of the spirit is added.

Retain the fifty capable men, requested search, hypothetical spirit removal, and all three possible destinations: Jordan, mountains and hills. A spirit of the Lord preserves the inherited indefinite reading; the scenario is the prophets' conjecture, not the narrator's assertion.
column3: Is a spirit of the Lord or the Spirit of the Lord preferable for the anarthrous expression here, and should the future prohibition remain Do not send them?

column2: Retain the pressure until Elisha was ashamed, his permission, fifty searchers, three days and failure to find Elijah. The emotion is not replaced with weariness alone, and no conclusion about Elijah's location is added.
Retain the return to Elisha while he remained in Jericho and his reminder that he had said not to go. The negative question recalls the actual prior prohibition rather than introducing a new rebuke.

Retain the good settlement, as the lord sees, bad waters and land bereaved of offspring. Lowercase lord addresses Elisha; the childlessness image is left broader than sterile crops alone, given the death/loss wording in verse 21.
column3: Does the bereaved-land expression refer primarily to miscarriage, failed produce or both; can a more idiomatic rendering preserve that range?

column2: Retain the new small water jar, salt placed there and the bringing of it to Elisha. Small represents the diminutive form rather than inventing an exact capacity; the object brought is inferred from the preceding command.

Retain the water outlet, thrown salt and the Lord's declaration I have healed, followed by no further death or loss of offspring from there. The future absence is not made into an instruction for water treatment, and the two consequences remain distinct.
Retain the waters' healed state through this day according to Elisha's word. Have remained healed naturally expresses the continuing result without dating this day to the modern reading occasion.

Retain small children for paidaria mikra and their repeated Go up, with baldhead stated once between the commands. The selected wording does not identify them as adult attackers or specify their intentions beyond mocking.

Retain the turn, sight, curse in the Lord's name, presentative, two bears, woodland and forty-two children torn open. The text is not softened or amplified into an explicit statement that all forty-two died; the outcome verb describes tearing.
column3: The precise turn-back phrase is awkward, but no different target group or motive should be supplied to resolve its difficulty.

column2: Retain the route from there to Mount Carmel and from there back to Samaria. The repeated departure markers close the itinerary without adding how long Elisha remained at either place.
